utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to begin by insuring that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Tolimir, can you hear the proceedings in a language that understand? Mr. Tolimir? You -- I see that you can hear the proceedings in a language you understand. Thank you. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILANINIA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Nema Milaninia on behalf of the Prosecution, here with my colleague Mr. Todd Schneider and our Case Manager Ms. Djurdja Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Appearances by the parties. The Prosecutor, I suppose you would say more or less the same thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you are self-representing, and I believe that Mr. Aleksandar Gajic has been granted the right of audience in the courtroom. Thank you. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes: First it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 5 July, 2013; thus, the Status Conference is taking place before the expiration of the 120 days period specified in the Rule 65 bis (B). Today's Status Conference was scheduled by the Scheduling Order issued on 17th September, 2013. Situation and health of the appellant. Let me now inquire into Mr. Tolimir's health. If you wish, this discussion can take place in a closed session. Would you like me to close the session, Mr. Tolimir, or no need? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused be asked to speak into the microphone, please, because we have difficulty hearing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I am so sorry. Would you like for the discussion, I had a question about your health and the question -- THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And the question is whether you would like -- THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] There is no need to go into closed session. I can say this in open session, that my health is as it ever was. I do not take any medication because there is no need for it. And I do hope the situation will obtain and I hope that with God's will we will bring this trial to an end. This is something we ourselves wish for. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. I am very pleased to hear that your health is as good as ever. So let me now turn to the procedural history of the case. On 4 September, 2013, the Appeals Chamber granted a motion by Mr. Tolimir for variation of the grounds of appeal and amendment of his appeal brief and ordered Mr. Tolimir to file an amended Notice of Appeal within five days of the date of issuance of the decision and a consolidated appeal brief within 20 days of the filing of the decision. By the same decision, the Appeals Chamber ordered the Prosecution to file a response brief within 21 days of the filing of the consolidated appeal brief. Mr. Tolimir filed his amended Notice of Appeal on 9 September, 2013, and a confidential version of his consolidated appeal brief on 24th September, 2013. The Prosecution filed a confidential version of its response brief on 16 October, 2013. Mr. Tolimir's reply brief is due on 31 October, 2013. On 25 October, 2013, Mr. Tolimir filed a motion for extension of time for the filing of his reply brief, requesting that I allow him to file his reply brief within 10 days of the filing of the B/C/S translation of the Prosecution's response brief. Alternatively, Mr. Tolimir requests that I grant him a seven-day extension for the filing of his reply brief and allow him, if necessary, to file an amended reply brief within 10 days of the filing of the B/C/S translation of the Prosecution's response brief. Tolimir submits that he's self-represented, that he does not understand the English language, that he has only one legal advisor, that the time for consultations with his legal advisor is limited, and that his legal advisor has been engaged in reviewing material recently disclosed by the Prosecution. Mr. Milaninia, I am wondering whether I could ask you to file a response, if any, by close of business tomorrow, 29 October, in which case I would render a decision shortly after receipt of your response.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILANINIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it satisfies the Court, we can actually give of our position today, which is that the Prosecution does not intend to object to Mr. Tolimir's motion. And as to the alternatives that Mr. Tolimir has posited, we take no position and we leave it to the wisdom of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In this case I will issue my decision now orally. It will save paper work and efforts to all the parties. In my view, the circumstances advanced by Mr. Tolimir constitute good cause for granting him a seven-day extension for the filing of his reply brief. I note that such an extension will not impact the overall time necessary for consideration of this appeal. Pursuant to Rules 127(A)(i) and 127(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, I hereby allow Mr. Tolimir to file his reply brief not later than 7 November 2013. Should Mr. Tolimir wish to file an amended version of his reply brief following the filing of the B/C/S translation of the Prosecution's response brief, he shall do so by motion within 10 days of the filing of the B/C/S translation of the Prosecution's response brief. So this is my ruling on the most recent request by Mr. Tolimir. So let me now ask the parties whether they have any other issues they would like to raise at this time. Mr. Tolimir, anything you would like to raise? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have nothing to raise. Greetings to everyone and I wish them success in the work in this trial. God-speed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILANINIA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution has no further issues at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Thank you, the Prosecutor. Since there are no other matters to be raised, I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close.
